thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: RESERVED_POOL_THROTTLE for tenant=nimbusapps cluster=dedicated-us-west1 at 06:12 UTC. Priority: high. Links: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/1749501234 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident INC-7842 created and routed to eng-oncall. Escalation policy: dedicated-tenants.

ajay_kumar: acked. I'm taking pager. What's current impact?

ev an_s: seeing 20–30% of requests 500s + latencies 1.2s -> 3s for /v1/generate forwarded to the reserved pool. Errors spike correlates with queue depth.

maria_rodriguez: confirm: tenant is on Reserved Pool RP-nimbus-03. Metrics show backlog on node gpu-07 and kvcache evictions. 

tara_ops: logs show repeated "insufficient tokens" and "burstbackpressure" traces. Autoscale not triggering; quota markers hit.

ajay_kumar: quick mitigation plan: 1) shift traffic for nimbusapps -> fallback pool (shared-hosted-lowcost) for non-SLA-critical routes, 2) bump reserved pool capacity by +2 GPUs, 3) enable temporary relaxed batching. Who can run capacity patch?

ev an_s: I can run the patch. Doing small increase to avoid noisy flapping. Running command: ```kubectl -n dedicated patch reservedpool rp-nimbus-03 --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":5}}'```

maria_rodriguez: also flip routing policy for tenant nimbusapps -> route_override:nimbus-fallback (5% canary -> then 100%) to reduce pressure. I'll push config.

incident-bot: Pager update: INC-7842 assigned to ajay_kumar.

ajay_kumar: capacity patch applied. Observability: queue depth started falling after 45s. Latency tail down from 3s -> 900ms for most requests. Error rate down ~70%.

ev an_s: routing switch deployed: canary 10% -> 100% over 2m. Confirming KV cache state kept consistent for most sessions; some cold hits expected.

maria_rodriguez: notifying support to tell customer NimbusApps about degraded latency window and mitigation steps. Draft message: "We detected a reserved pool throttle affecting a subset of requests; we routed traffic to a fallback pool and increased capacity. You may see a small number of degraded responses during the window 06:10–06:22 UTC."

tara_ops: adding runbook note: suspected root cause - autoscaler missed scale due to recent config drift in the throttle thresholds. Opening follow-up ticket to adjust thresholds and add synthetic probe.

ajay_kumar: Pager update -> paging team: handoff incoming. I'll stay for the next 30 min then hand to maria for post-incident and oncall.

incident-bot: INC-7842: status=mitigated, severity=major. Time to mitigation: ~10m.

emails: pagerduty note auto-sent to stakeholders.

maria_rodriguez: I'm taking post-incident. Please drop any logs/error traces you want included. Key artifacts: kube patch diff, routing override commit id, graphs (queue depth, p50/p99 latency), and customer support message.

ajay_kumar: adding a quick snippet for postmortem: "Immediate cause: reserved pool reached configured throttle at peak burst. Contributing: autoscaler threshold misalignment + KV eviction spike. Mitigation: temporary capacity bump + routing fallback. Next actions: tighten scaling probe, reduce config drift by CI gating, add early-warning alert at 60% queue depth."

ev an_s: uploading logs to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-7842/ and linking in the incident doc.

maria_rodriguez: thanks. I'll create the postmortem draft and ping oncall for review. Closing pager now but keeping incident thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
